newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon court sentences drug gang to jail.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon court sentences drug gang to jail.

text.p: A Beirut court sentenced on Tuesday a wealthy Lebanese businessman and his gang to jail for smuggling drugs to the Netherlands and Canada, judicial sources said.

The five years in prison for leading the gang was the third jail sentence imposed on Beirut businessman Ghassan Matraji in a year. He could spend up to 10 years and nine months behind bars if an appeal against the rulings fails.

The sources said the court ordered jail sentences of up to three years for five accomplices, including Canadian Margaret Zelestra, who received 19 months and her Lebanese husband Ahmad Watfah who received two years.
The rulings can be appealed at a higher court.
All the accused, including Matraji, are in custody. The court ordered eight years in jail in absentia for five other accomplices who are on the run.
If they surrender or get arrested, they would be retried under Lebanese laws.

In the original November 1995 indictment, Matraji was charged of having "undertaken big smuggling operations so that his name became known among local and international security organs in the trafficking world."

Last month, he was convicted of dollar forgery for smuggling to Turkey and African states. He was sentenced to five years in prison. A year earlier, he was sentenced to nine months in jail by a military court in Beirut for smuggling arms to and from Lebanon during the 1975-1990 civil war.
